land.text: the whole Grand Duchy of Cliopatria's last shape, drawn inside the Jagiellonian realm from 1450

successors.note: Cliopatria's Grand Duchy row ends in 1449 and its House of Jagiellon row begins in 1450; the Grand Duchy itself lasted to the Third Partition of 24 October 1795 (infobox), as a distinct state inside the Jagiellonian union and the Commonwealth. The end year 1449 is the map's, not the state's.

rulers.name: Vytautas the Great
rulers.title: Grand Duke

rulers.name: Švitrigaila
rulers.title: Grand Duke

rulers.note: The page: King of Poland and Grand Duke from 29 June 1440 to 7 June 1492; the strip stops at 1449, the end of Cliopatria's row.

166,476 km2 in Cliopatria: Lithuania proper, Black Ruthenia, Polotsk, Vitebsk and Minsk. Repair pass: the Principality of Polotsk page has Polotsk 'a vassal of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' in 1240 and 'officially' Lithuanian only in 1307 (Polotsk dossier: its own shape 1241-1306), and the Mindaugas page has Tautvilas receive Polotsk 'as a fiefdom' after 1255, so Polotsk and the Vitebsk land are drawn as vassal land, not as direct territory; the same reading is applied to the Minsk land (confidence 1). The shape therefore holds the 1260 outline for 1250-1259. The Mindaugas page's 1255 transfer of Black Ruthenia to Roman, Daniel's son, is not explained and the Navahrudak and Hrodna part is left as drawn.

correction.text: Lithuania proper and Black Ruthenia only: the 1260 shape holds for 1250-1259, without the Polotsk, Vitebsk and Minsk land the Cliopatria 1250 shape adds (those lands are Lithuanian vassals, see the vassal events of 1240 and 1250)

keyframe_review.note: 90,777 km2 against the infobox's '1260: 200,000 km2' (main page): ratio 2.2 on this shape alone. The gap is the Polotsk, Vitebsk and Minsk land: from 1260 Cliopatria draws it as its own Principality of Minsk row (98,755 km2, to 1313), and 90,777 + 98,755 = 189,532 km2 is within 6% of the infobox. The infobox figure is therefore followed as Lithuanian-dominated land and the Cliopatria 'loss' of 1260 is not taken as a loss: the Polotsk page has Polotsk a vassal from 1240 to 1307, no page opened records a Lithuanian withdrawal in 1260 (the Mindaugas page has only Durbe, the break with the Livonian Order in 1261 and his death in 1263), and the Polotsk dossier keeps Polotsk independent-as-vassal to 1307. The shape stays the direct territory (Lithuania proper and Black Ruthenia, where the main page has Traidenis 'strengthened Lithuanian control in Black Ruthenia', 1269-1282); the vassal events carry the rest.
91,051 km2: the same lands as 1260-1271 (Lithuania proper and Black Ruthenia). Traidenis's rule 1269-1282 and the move of the capital to Kernavė 'after 1279' (infobox) do not change the shape.

correction.text: years only: shape unchanged for 1294-1306; see _1307

correction.text: the 1294 shape plus Polotsk, annexed around 1307

correction.text: years only: the 1314 shape unchanged, without Kyiv, for 1314-1320; see _1321

keyframe_review.note: 190,067 km2 (Lithuania proper, Black Ruthenia, Polotsk, Vitebsk, Minsk). Holds for 1314-1320 without Kyiv: 'In 1321, Gediminas captured Kiev' (main page), so Kyiv is added only by the new keyframe _1321 (1321-1325). Cliopatria draws Kyiv from 1363, and the Blue Waters page says Lithuania then 'finalized their conquest of the Principality of Kiev', so the hold on Kyiv between 1321 and 1362 was partial. Vitebsk is placed in Algirdas's 1318 marriage on the Algirdas page, four years after this shape begins.
New keyframe: the 1314 shape plus Kyiv for 1321-1325 ('In 1321, Gediminas captured Kiev', main page); the 1326 and later keyframes carry Kyiv on.

282,660 km2: adds Pinsk, Turov, Brest and the border of Volhynia to the 1314 shape. The main page says that in 1320 most western Rus' principalities 'were either vassalized or annexed by Lithuania'; the Gediminas page says the conquest dates 'impossible to follow' for 1325-1340. Kyiv is added as for 1314.

292,674 km2: Cliopatria adds Lutsk and more of Volhynia when its Galicia-Volhynia row ends (1351). The Gediminas page lists Lubart's duchy as 'Lutsk, Volhynia' without a date. Holds for 1352-1356; Kyiv is added; Chernigov and Bryansk follow from 1357 (new keyframe _1357). Repair pass: the Galicia-Volhynia Wars page has the fall-1352 truce 'rather favourable to the Lithuanians' and the Kingdom page has 'Eastern Volhynia together with Kiev' under Lithuanian control 1352-66, which is why 1352 (not the page's 1349) is the year of the Volhynian gain.

union.text: the Chernigov land with Bryansk, under Lithuanian control around 1357-1358

correction.text: the 1352 shape plus Kyiv, Chernigov and Bryansk

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Blue Waters page says most of the Principality of Chernigov, 'including Bryansk, fell under Lithuanian control around 1357–1358', before the battle; Cliopatria draws these lands only from 1363.

763,775 km2: Kyiv, Podolia, Pereyaslavl, Chernigov and the Black Sea coast. The Blue Waters page: the victory brought 'Kyiv and a large part of present-day Ukraine, including sparsely populated Podolia and Dykra', and Lithuania 'gained access to the Black Sea'. Autumn 1362 or 1363 on that page; 1362 on the Algirdas page. Smolensk is not in the shape (its own Cliopatria row runs to 1406).

815,402 km2, +52,000 km2 on the 1363 shape. Repair pass, split by cells: about 157 of the 228 new cells (some 40,000 km2, 30.6-34.9 E, 55.8-57.7 N: Velikiye Luki, Toropets, Nelidovo) are the north strip the Smolensk dossier records as leaving Smolensk's shape in 1375; the other 71 (about 18,000 km2, 25.4-29.9 E, 46.7-49.7 N) are the Kamianets/Podolia part. No page dates either: the Smolensk page is silent on 1375, and the Podolia page has Algirdas free Podolia from the Golden Horde in 1362 and 'western Podolia, including Kamieniec Podolski' pass under Polish sovereignty in 1366. The Algirdas page says at his death in May 1377 the state reached 'from the present Baltic states to the Black Sea' and 'to within 80 kilometres (50 miles) of Moscow'.

811,346 km2. Union of Krewo: the infobox gives 14 August 1385, the body 1386 (the page is inconsistent); Jogaila 'became King of Poland in 1386'. A personal union, no territory moves; Cliopatria's umbrella '(Polish-Lithuania Kingdom)' runs 1395-1449 and is not territory.

806,616 km2 plus Smolensk (about 84,000 km2): 'When Vytautas captured Smolensk in 1395, Vasily offered no resistance' (Smolensk page), and Smolensk revolted in 1401 (new keyframe _1401). Cliopatria draws Smolensk with its own row, not with Lithuania, in these years. Two losses happen inside these years: Samogitia, ceded in 1398, and the Black Sea coast, lost at the Vorskla in 1399; Cliopatria draws both losses from 1402 (three to four years late, left as drawn). The Vytautas page: in 1398 'Lithuania spanned from the Baltic Sea to the Black Sea'. The Vorskla page puts Yury's revolt right 'after the battle' of 1399 ('not recaptured for five years'); the Smolensk page dates the revolt 1401, which is the year used.

686,731 km2: Samogitia and the Black Sea coast are gone (Salynas 1398, Vorskla 1399). Smolensk, 'not re-conquered by Lithuanians until 1404' (Vytautas page), is still outside; Cliopatria adds it with its own row's end in 1407, three years late, left as drawn.
761,211 km2: with Smolensk (1404). Samogitia returned for the lifetimes of Jogaila and Vytautas at the Peace of Thorn on 1 February 1411 (Thorn page) but Cliopatria draws it back only from 1415.

801,567 km2: Samogitia is back (Thorn 1411: 'only for the lifetimes of Polish King Jogaila and Lithuanian Grand Duke Vytautas'). Memel is taken out: after Melno 1422 'Samogitia was returned to Lithuania in perpetuity, while the city of Memel ... stayed with the Order' (Vytautas page), so Lithuania never held it; the contest of 1414-1422 over Memel stays in the ledger.

keyframe_review.note: 801,213 km2 against the infobox's 930,000 km2 for 1430 (main page): ratio 0.86, within the usual margin. The Vytautas page: at Melno in 1422 'Samogitia was returned to Lithuania in perpetuity, while Memel stayed with the Order', so Memel is taken out of the shape (as of the 1415 shape too: Lithuania never held it, so there is no loss in 1422).

746,428 km2: Cliopatria drops Kamianets and most of Podolia and a little of Volhynia in 1431. The Civil War page: 'Polish nobles believed a 1411 agreement gave Lithuania control only during Vytautas's lifetime' and Sigismund 'later made territorial concessions to Poland in both areas' (Podolia and Volhynia), undated. From 1432 the page puts Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia with Švitrigaila; Cliopatria draws one Lithuania, and the ledger records the split. Repair pass: the page's date for the concessions is 1432 (Grodno), 1431 is the Cliopatria shape year.

746,628 km2, unchanged. Casimir IV was 'elected as the Grand Duke of Lithuania upon his arrival to Vilnius on 29 June 1440' and became King of Poland in 1447 (main page); the personal union does not move a border.

The infobox gives 'Sovereign state (1236–1386, 1440–1447, 1492–1501)' and the Mindaugas page says the Livonian Rhymed Chronicle calls him ruler of all Lithuania in 1236, though 'His path to this title is not clear'. ledger.note: 1240: 'Grand Prince Yaroslav Vsevolodovich expelled them the following year' (Smolensk page).

region.text: Polotsk and the Vitebsk land, the principality the Polotsk dossier draws for 1241-1306

ledger.note: 1240: Polotsk becomes a vassal of Lithuania. 'in 1240 Polotsk became a vassal of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' (Principality of Polotsk page). The Mindaugas page is vaguer and later (Polotsk gained after the coronation, undated; Tautvilas 'received Polatsk as a fiefdom' after 1255) and the main page has Polotsk annexed only 'around 1307', so the year is the one page's and the relation is vassalage, not rule. Cliopatria draws the land in Lithuania's shape for 1250-1259 and not in 1260-1313; replaces the 1250 gain and the 1260 loss of the first version.

region.text: Minsk and its land, the Minsk principality of Cliopatria's 1241 shape

ledger.note: 1250: Cliopatria draws Minsk inside Lithuania for 1250-1259 and, from 1260 to 1313, as its own Principality of Minsk row (98,755 km2, covering Minsk, Polotsk and Vitebsk) whose area the infobox ('1260: 200,000 km2') counts with Lithuania's 90,777 km2. No page opened mentions Minsk under Mindaugas; read as Lithuanian-dominated land (vassal), confidence 1. Replaces the 1250 gain and 1260 loss of the first version.

1251: Lithuania becomes a kingdom. 'a papal bull proclaimed the creation of the Kingdom of Lithuania' in 1251; Mindaugas is 'crowned as King of Lithuania on 6 July 1253'. The infobox gives 'Kingdom of Lithuania: 1251–1263'. The Mindaugas page dates the bulls 17 July 1251 and the crowning to summer 1253, the exact day being disputed.

1263: Mindaugas is assassinated and the Kingdom of Lithuania ends. 'assassinated Mindaugas and his two sons, Ruklys and Rupeikis, in 1263' (main page); the Mindaugas page infobox gives 12 September 1263.
1279: the capital moves to Kernavė. Infobox: 'Kernavė (after 1279 – before 1316 or 1321)'.

The Polotsk page: 'It officially became part of Lithuania in 1307, though it retained some degree of local autonomy until the 1390s'; the vassalage since 1240 ends here.

region.text: Kyiv, captured by Gediminas in 1321

ledger.note: 1321: Gediminas captures Kyiv. 'In 1321, Gediminas captured Kiev.' The Gediminas page has him defeat Stanislav at the Irpin and install Theodor and Algimantas, and the Blue Waters page says the conquest was only 'finalized' in 1362 or 1363, so the hold was partial; Cliopatria draws Kyiv with Lithuania only from 1363.
1323: Vilnius becomes the capital. Infobox: 'Vilnius (from 1323)'; the Gediminas page says 'in c. 1320'.

The main page says Vytenis sought to 'capture the principalities of Pinsk and Turov' and the Gediminas page says the dates of the conquests of 1325-1340 are 'impossible to follow'; the year is Cliopatria's. ledger.note: 1326: a strip on Masovia's north-eastern edge goes to Lithuania. The Trojden page: on 2 January 1326 the Masovian dukes agreed with the Teutonic Order at Brodnica, 'which led to a short conflict with Poland and its ally Lithuania'; it names no land and no transfer, so the year and the 2 cells (506 km2, inside Cliopatria's 1326 growth) are Cliopatria's. region.text: Volhynia, fought over by Liubartas, Casimir III and Louis I

ledger.note: 1349: Poland and Hungary occupy Galicia-Volhynia and Volhynia is contested. 'Only in 1349, after the occupation of Galicia-Volhynia by an allied Polish-Hungarian force' (Kingdom page; the timeline entry reads 'Galicia annexed (patrimonial) by Poland and Hungary, Volhynia - Lithuania'). The Galicia-Volhynia Wars page runs the succession wars 1340-1392 (see /wars).

region.text: Lutsk and the Volhynian lands added in the 1352 shape

ledger.note: 1352: Lithuania holds Lutsk and eastern Volhynia. The Galicia-Volhynia Wars page: 'Another truce, rather favourable to the Lithuanians, was signed in fall 1352'; the 1366 treaty left Liubartas 'only eastern Volhynia with Lutsk'; the Kingdom page: 'Eastern Volhynia together with Kiev came under Lithuanian control, 1352-66'. The counterpart's own dossier dates the loss to 1349 (Kingdom page timeline: 'Galicia annexed (patrimonial) by Poland and Hungary, Volhynia - Lithuania'); that is not used here because the pages show Casimir III holding Western Volhynia and Liubartas keeping only the east until the 1352 truce, which is also the year of Cliopatria's shape. Gediminas page: Liubartas's appanage was 'Lutsk, Volhynia' under Gediminas (d. 1341), undated.

region.text: Smolensk and Rzhev, taken by Algirdas in 1356 and contested with Moscow to 1359

ledger.note: 1356: Algirdas captures Smolensk and Bryansk. 'Grand Duke Algirdas of Lithuania captured Bryansk and Smolensk in 1356' (Smolensk page); Ivan II of Moscow gave no help to his son-in-law's side, and in 1358 a Moscow, Mozhaysk and Tver expedition drove the Lithuanians out of Rzhev. Mirror of the Smolensk dossier's contest.

region.text: Smolensk and Rzhev, taken by Algirdas in 1356 and contested with Moscow to 1359

ledger.note: 1359: Algirdas 'launched an attack, regaining control of Smolensk and Rzhev while taking control of Mstislavl' (Smolensk page; the year 1359 follows from the page's 'the following year' after 1358). The Smolensk dossier also records a south-western band (Gomel, Orsha, Krichev, Mogilev) as lost to Lithuania in 1359 at confidence 1; Cliopatria draws it Lithuanian from 1363, inside the Blue Waters gain.

minus.text: the Chernigov land with Bryansk, under Lithuanian control around 1357-1358

region.text: Kyiv, Pereyaslavl, Podolia and Dykra, down to the Black Sea

ledger.note: 1363: Lithuania takes Kyiv, Podolia and the road to the Black Sea from the Golden Horde. The victory brought 'Kyiv and a large part of present-day Ukraine, including sparsely populated Podolia and Dykra' under Lithuanian control, and 'It is believed that Algirdas further conquered territories of the former Principality of Pereyaslavl'; Algirdas left his son Vladimir in Kyiv, and Podolia was entrusted to Karijotas's sons. The region also holds the south-western band of Smolensk's land (Gomel, Orsha, Krichev, Mogilev) that the Smolensk dossier records as lost to Lithuania in 1359 (confidence 1); the Smolensk page names only Mstislavl.

region.text: Volhynia, fought over by Liubartas, Casimir III and Louis I

ledger.note: 1366: the treaty of fall 1366 divides Volhynia. 'In fall 1366, a treaty was signed': Liubartas 'retained only eastern Volhynia with Lutsk'. The page has Lithuania capture 'all of Volhynia, including Volodymyr' after Casimir's death in 1370 and Lithuania in control of Volhynia at Ostrow in 1392; Cliopatria draws one Lithuanian shape for the whole period, so the Polish hold on western Volhynia in 1366-1370 is not drawn.

region.text: the north strip (Velikiye Luki, Toropets, Nelidovo) that Cliopatria moves from Smolensk's shape to Lithuania's in 1375

ledger.note: 1375: about 40,000 km2 in the north (30.6-34.9 E, 55.8-57.7 N) pass from Smolensk's shape to Lithuania's. Mirror of the Smolensk dossier's loss of 1375 (confidence 1 there too): the Smolensk page, reopened, does not mention Velikiye Luki, Toropets, Nelidovo or any 1375 transfer, so the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the south of the 1375 growth: Kamianets and the Podolian land (about 18,000 km2, 25.4-29.9 E, 46.7-49.7 N)

ledger.note: 1375: Cliopatria adds Kamianets and Podolian land in the south. No page dates it: the Podolia page has Algirdas free Podolia from the Golden Horde in 1362 and 'western Podolia, including Kamieniec Podolski' pass under Polish sovereignty in 1366, and the only 1375 item on it is the founding of the Catholic diocese of Kamianets. No state is named for the land in 1375, so the counterpart is 'nobody' (the Golden Horde is the 1362 holder); the year is Cliopatria's.

minus.text: Mozhaysk and its land (Volokolamsk to the north), a Moscow possession from 1304 on the Principality of Moscow page; a lon/lat radius because the gazetteer has no 'Mozhaysk'

region.text: Smolensk and its land as Cliopatria draws the 1375 shape, without Mozhaysk

ledger.note: 1395: Vytautas captures Smolensk. 'When Vytautas captured Smolensk in 1395, Vasily offered no resistance' and accepted the annexation the following year (Smolensk page). The Vytautas page gives no year for the capture. Mirror of the Smolensk dossier's loss of 1395.

region.text: Samogitia, the ancestral province Vytautas ceded to the Teutonic Knights

ledger.note: 1398: Vytautas cedes Samogitia to the Teutonic Knights. 'ceded his ancestral province of Samogitia to the knights' by the Treaty of Salynas; the page adds that in 1404 at Raciąż 'Samogitia was transferred to the Teutonic Knights', and the Thorn page that it was under Teutonic control 'since the Peace of Raciąż (1404)'. Cliopatria draws the loss from 1402.

union.text: Samogitia, the ancestral province Vytautas ceded to the Teutonic Knights
Memel (Klaipėda), which 'stayed with the Order' at Melno

region.text: the Black Sea coast and the southern steppe, lost to the Tatars

ledger.note: August 1399: Vytautas is crushed at the Vorskla and loses the Black Sea coast. 'Lithuania loses the Black Sea coast and southern part of the Wild Fields to the Tatars' (infobox; the infobox says 12 August, the text 5 August). Cliopatria draws the loss from 1402.

minus.text: Mozhaysk and its land (Volokolamsk to the north), a Moscow possession from 1304 on the Principality of Moscow page; a lon/lat radius because the gazetteer has no 'Mozhaysk'

region.text: Smolensk and its land as Cliopatria draws the 1402 shape, without Mozhaysk

ledger.note: 1401: Smolensk revolts and leaves Lithuania. 'In 1401, the people of Smolensk launched a revolt against Lithuanian rule' and recalled Yury; Vytautas 'reasserted control three years later' (Smolensk page). The Vytautas page: 'Smolensk was retaken by its hereditary ruler, George of Smolensk, and not re-conquered by Lithuanians until 1404'; the Vorskla page places the revolt right after the battle of 1399 ('not recaptured for five years'), two years before the Smolensk page's date. Mirror of the Smolensk dossier's gain of 1401.

region.text: Smolensk

ledger.note: 1404: Vytautas retakes Smolensk. It 'was retaken by its hereditary ruler, George of Smolensk, and not re-conquered by Lithuanians until 1404'; the Vorskla page says Smolensk, Novgorod and Pskov rebelled after 1399 and Smolensk 'stayed out of Lithuanian hands for about five years'. Cliopatria's Smolensk row runs to 1406 and Lithuania's shape includes it from 1407.

region.text: Samogitia, the ancestral province Vytautas ceded to the Teutonic Knights

ledger.note: May 1409: Samogitia rises against the Order. 'In May 1409, a local uprising began there. Vytautas supported it, and Poland also backed the Samogitian cause', and the war that followed ended at Grunwald in June 1410.

region.text: Samogitia, the ancestral province Vytautas ceded to the Teutonic Knights

ledger.note: 1 February 1411: the Peace of Thorn returns Samogitia to Lithuania for two lifetimes. The Knights gave up their claim 'only for the lifetimes of Polish King Jogaila and Lithuanian Grand Duke Vytautas'. Cliopatria draws it back from 1415.

region.text: Samogitia, the ancestral province Vytautas ceded to the Teutonic Knights

ledger.note: 1 February 1411: the war of 1409-1411 ends with the Peace of Thorn.

region.text: Memel (Klaipėda), which 'stayed with the Order' at Melno

ledger.note: 1414: the Hunger War over the north bank of the Neman and Memel. Vytautas claimed 'the land north of the Neman River, including Memel'; in May 1413 the arbitrator Benedict Makrai awarded it to Lithuania, 'The Knights refused, and the inconclusive Hunger War broke out in 1414.'

region.text: Memel (Klaipėda), which 'stayed with the Order' at Melno

ledger.note: 1422: the Treaty of Melno ends the Samogitian dispute. 'Samogitia was returned to Lithuania in perpetuity, while Memel stayed with the Order.'

region.text: the land the 1431 shape no longer holds (Podolia and a corner of Volhynia)

ledger.note: 1431: Cliopatria drops Kamianets, most of Podolia and a corner of Volhynia (1431 is Cliopatria's shape year). The Civil War page puts Sigismund's 'territorial concessions to Poland in disputed Podolia and Volhynia' in its account of the Union of Grodno (15 October 1432), not in 1431, and names no lands; the Podolia page has 'Podolia' incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland after Vytautas died (1430) with its eastern part, Bracław, remaining with Lithuania. The year therefore lies between the pages' 1430 and 1432; the land is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Volhynia, around Lutsk

ledger.note: 25 June 1431: Poland invades Volhynia. 'Poland invades Volhynia on 25 June' in the Lutsk War over the inheritance of Vytautas.

region.text: Volhynia, around Lutsk

ledger.note: 1 September 1431: a truce at Staryi Chortoryisk ends the Lutsk War.

region.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, Švitrigaila's side

ledger.note: 31 August 1432: the coup that makes Sigismund Kęstutaitis Grand Duke splits the state. Sigismund's supporters held 'the Lithuanian lands, Samogitia, Trakai Voivodeship, and Minsk'; Švitrigaila's supporters held Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia. The page dates the coup to 31 August 1432 and gives no dates for the other side's hold.

region.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia, recovered from Švitrigaila's side

ledger.note: 1438: Švitrigaila withdraws to Moldavia and his side ends. 'Švitrigaila withdraws to Moldavia' in 1438 (the lead says he surrendered in 1437, after his army was beaten at Wiłkomierz in September 1435); the Švitrigaila page has him propose in September 1437 to rule the lands that still backed him, 'chiefly Kiev and Volhynia', which the Polish Senate did not ratify. Sigismund rules until his assassination in 1440.

region.text: the Grand Duchy of Cliopatria's last shape

ledger.note: 1449: the Grand Duchy's last Cliopatria shape ends and the lands pass into the Jagiellonian realm. The Grand Duchy itself lasted until 'Third Partition: 24 October 1795' (infobox), as a part of the union and the Commonwealth; Casimir IV was Grand Duke from 1440 and King of Poland from 1447.

wars.name: Battle of Durbe (Livonian Order against Samogitians and Lithuanians)
wars.outcome: The Order lost Skuodas in 1259 and Durbe in 1260; Mindaugas 'broke peace with the Livonian Order' in 1261. No Lithuanian land changed hands that the page records.

wars.name: Lithuanian wars against the Teutonic and Livonian Orders under Gediminas
wars.outcome: Gediminas 'allied himself with the Tatars against the Teutonic Order in 1319', made peace with the Livonian Order on 2 October 1323, and the war resumed after the Order murdered his delegate in 1325; the page records a battle at Bayernburg in 1337. No change of border.

wars.name: Battle of Blue Waters

minus.text: the Chernigov land with Bryansk, under Lithuanian control around 1357-1358

zones.text: Kyiv, Pereyaslavl, Podolia and Dykra, down to the Black Sea

wars.outcome: Lithuanian victory over the Golden Horde: Kyiv, Podolia and a large part of today's Ukraine under Lithuanian control, with access to the Black Sea.
wars.note: Autumn 1362 or 1363 (Blue Waters page); 1362 on the Algirdas and main pages.

wars.name: Galicia-Volhynia Wars (succession wars of 1340-1392)
wars.outcome: After Yuri II Boleslav was poisoned in April 1340 Poland, Hungary and Lithuania fought over his lands: a truce 'rather favourable to the Lithuanians' in fall 1352, a treaty in fall 1366 that left Liubartas 'only eastern Volhynia with Lutsk', Lithuanian capture of 'all of Volhynia, including Volodymyr' after Casimir's death in 1370, Galicia attached to Poland 'for good' in 1387, and the Ostrow Agreement of 1392, after which 'Lithuania controlled Volhynia'.
wars.note: Only the contest of 1349-1366 and the Volhynian gain of 1352 are drawn; the Polish hold on Volodymyr in 1366-1370 is not (Cliopatria draws one Lithuanian shape).

wars.name: Lithuanian-Muscovite War (1368-1372)
wars.outcome: Algirdas 'besieged Moscow in 1368 and 1370'; no border change is recorded on the page.

wars.name: Battle of the Vorskla River

union.text: Samogitia, the ancestral province Vytautas ceded to the Teutonic Knights
Memel (Klaipėda), which 'stayed with the Order' at Melno

zones.text: the Black Sea coast and southern steppe

wars.outcome: A decisive Golden Horde victory under Edigu and Temür Qutlugh: Vytautas barely escaped and 'Lithuania loses the Black Sea coast and southern part of the Wild Fields to the Tatars'.
wars.note: 12 August 1399 in the infobox, 5 August in the text.

wars.name: Great War (Polish-Lithuanian-Teutonic War of 1409-1411)

zones.text: Samogitia, the ancestral province Vytautas ceded to the Teutonic Knights

wars.outcome: The Samogitian uprising of May 1409 grew into war; after Grunwald (June 1410) the Peace of Thorn of 1 February 1411 gave Samogitia to Lithuania for the lifetimes of Jogaila and Vytautas and returned Dobrzyń Land to Poland.

wars.name: Hunger War

zones.text: Memel (Klaipėda), which 'stayed with the Order' at Melno

wars.outcome: An inconclusive war over the north bank of the Neman and Memel after the Knights refused Makrai's award of May 1413; the dispute was 'not resolved until the Treaty of Melno in 1422'.

wars.name: Lutsk War
wars.outcome: Poland invaded Volhynia on 25 June 1431 after Vytautas's death; a truce at Staryi Chortoryisk on 1 September 1431 ended it, and the Knights were defeated at Dąbki on 13 September.

wars.name: Lithuanian Civil War (1432-1438)

zones.text: Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia

wars.outcome: Sigismund Kęstutaitis, backed by Poland, defeated Švitrigaila, backed by the Teutonic Knights, at Wiłkomierz in September 1435; Švitrigaila surrendered in 1437 and withdrew to Moldavia in 1438; Sigismund was assassinated in 1440 and Casimir IV approved as hereditary hospodar.
wars.note: The page's lead says 1437, the body says Švitrigaila withdrew in 1438.

certainty.note: Frontiers with the Rus' principalities, the steppe and the Orders are approximate throughout; the Samogitian border with the Teutonic Order is fixed by treaty only from the Treaty of Melno in 1422 (Memel stayed with the Order), the one sharp line.

notes: Cliopatria's row starts 1220; the dossier starts the state in 1236 (infobox 'Sovereign state (1236–1386, ...)') and marks the 1220 shape wrong and the 1227 and 1241 shapes adjust (add Navahrudak and Hrodna from 1236). Page conflicts: the main page has Polotsk annexed 'around 1307', the Mindaugas page has it under Mindaugas in the 1230s-1240s; Cliopatria has it with Mindaugas 1250-1259, without it 1260-1313, with it from 1314. Kyiv: 1321 on the main page, 'finalized' 1362-63 on the Blue Waters page; Cliopatria draws it from 1363. Samogitia: 1398 (Salynas) and 1404 (Raciąż) on the Vytautas page, Teutonic control 'since 1404' on the Thorn page; Cliopatria draws the loss from 1402. The union of Krewo is dated 14 August 1385 in the infobox and 1386 in the body. Unexplained shape growth: 1375 (+52,000 km2), 1352 (Volhynia), 1326 (Brest). The 1432-1437 civil war: Švitrigaila's side holds Polotsk, Vitebsk, Smolensk, Kiev and Volhynia; counterpart svitrigaila-s-grand-duchy (a rebel dossier written by this batch from the Civil War and Švitrigaila pages). Masovia's dossier records a 1326 strip lost to Lithuania; the Trojden page was reopened in the repair pass and names no land, so the matching gain is recorded at confidence 1 from Cliopatria's two cells. The ruler strip comes from the List of Lithuanian monarchs (repair pass). Gazetteer: 'Hrodna' and 'Novogrudok' are places in the gazetteer; Black Ruthenia, Kernavė and Dykra are not. Repair pass of 2026-10-31 (reviewer findings): Polotsk and the Minsk land are vassals (1240/1250 to 1307/1314), no longer gained in 1250 and lost in 1260, so the 200,000 km2 infobox figure for 1260 is explained by the Minsk row (see _1260); Smolensk is held 1395-1400 and lost in 1401 (keyframes _1395 and _1401); Kyiv enters with the new keyframe _1321; Memel is removed from the 1415 shape and the 1422 'loss' is deleted; the 1375 growth is split into the Smolensk north strip and the Podolian south; the 1326 Masovian strip is carved out; 1352 stays the Volhynian year (the page's 1349 is not used, see the ledger note); the 1432/1431 date of the Podolia and Volhynia concessions is explained. Not done: the Polish hold on western Volhynia in 1366-1370 and the Smolensk band of 1359 are not drawn.
